Bob Readman too, was absent, having arrested a couple of housebreakers, so we must be content to make a real effort during the coming season to build up a really strong team c…

Jack Baker, our first man home, was the only one to get inside nine hours. Gordon Doubleday, who completed the course in 47 minutes less time than last year, won a handicap prize presented by Charlie Poulter.

Unfortunately Jack Baker was unable to get to the start, but even so we still had hopes of a place. After doing about 35 miles, however, Jack Bidgood was forced to retire with blistered feet and with the remaining men making a brave effort, we had again to be content with 4th place, Team honours going to Surrey W.C.
These included Pat Sapcote and Jack Baker. The unusual distance of the race got the team selectors guessing with the result that two of our “ B ” team men finished before the second “ A ” team man.

Scoring 16 a side, the match resulted in a win for the Club by 253 points to 275. George Oliver, with an allowance of 4.15, was first in the handicap with Jack Baker (6.0) 2nd and Pat Sapcote (3.45) 3rd.

Jack Baker came next but at the half distance George Bentley who owing to his recent heavy studying has been unable to get fit, retired. Ted Evans, walking as an individual at his own expense for experience sake, showed up to advantage.

Jack Baker and Pat Sapcote also had leg trouble and they too retired. It was good to see Harry Shields coming along with a determined look on his face, subsequently finishing 44th, in his first long distance walk, over 20 miles.
Unfortunately Jack Baker and Gordon Doubleday were compelled to retire owing to foot trouble before the halfway stage was reached and later, at 40 miles, Bill Urry was forced to give up.
Norton, one of our new members, did very well to finish in the centre of the field and should feel bucked at beating such old campaigners as Joe Wilson and Jack Baker.
Jack BAKER (Middlesex)
His 8th position, only 2:04 down on Middleton must have been one of his best ever performances. Gerry Cameron (not at his best) and the fast improving Jack Baker completed our scoring four.

Bob Barnes and Jack Baker followed up their Highgate outings with races the following week at Enfield and Bexley. Bob finished only 87 seconds behind K.Easlea (Enfield), clocking 54:35 over a seven mile course.
Never mind Ian, it happens to the best of them. Another son in regular training is John Baker (son of Jack). With over 300 senior members in the Club we should have a lot more!.
